transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-10-07 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes (recording)
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Liam O'Connor (Redwood SE), Carlos Vega (BlueAnchor - Head of MLOps), Nora Liu (BlueAnchor - Platform Eng), Samir Patel (BlueAnchor - Procurement)

Auto Summary (auto-gen, may be rough): go/no-go for renewal uplift, agree on pilot benchmarks, talk through private/VPC constraints, outline next steps and contract amendment timeline.

[00:00] Maya: Alright everyone thanks for joining, quick check, can you hear me okay?
[00:03] Nora: Yep, loud and clear.
[00:05] Carlos: Good, thanks Maya.
[00:07] Maya: Cool. High level agenda — 1) renewal numbers and uplift ask, 2) APAC and EU activation plan, 3) private/VPC constraints and hsm/kms questions, 4) next steps and timing. Anything to add?
[00:20] Samir: Procurement timeline — just to flag we'll need the amendment and pricing before 10/20. That's a hard date for our quarter close.
[00:26] Maya: Got it, we'll aim for that.
[00:28] Liam: I'll also run a bench with your 10k prompt set over the weekend, want to test p99 and cold-starts.
[00:33] Carlos: That would be great. We saw p99 spikes especially on the nightly batch -- sometimes tails to like 800-900 ms, which hurts user experience.
[00:41] Nora: And on the EU side we need data residency for audit logs, so the VPC/on-prem option is still on the table.
[00:47] Maya: Understood, Nora. Quick clarification, is the ask 30% uplift in reserved capacity plus some burst credits?
[00:52] Carlos: Yes — baseline 30% uplift, and then a burst pool equal to ~20% of baseline for seasonal peaks.
[00:59] Maya: Ok, that's helpful. Liam, any immediate concerns from runtime side?
[01:03] Liam: Not concerns, more clarifying — we need your typical sequence lengths and tokenization distribution. Also KV cache hit rates matter a lot in the cost numbers, we discussed KV cache earlier but in their runbooks sometimes it's 'K V cash' in the logs so we wanted to verify.
[01:20] Carlos: Heh, yeah our logs are messy. We'll export a sample. We do see cache hit rates dip during flash sales.
[01:27] Samir: On procurement, for burst accounting we prefer a credit pool model that can be invoiced monthly instead of upfront commit. Is that supported?
[01:34] Maya: We can do a mixed model — reserved monthly commit + a billed burst pool. We'll draft options.
[01:39] Nora: For the VPC pilot, security wants SOC2 type II evidence and ISO27001 checklist. Can you share the security pack?
[01:45] Maya: Yes, we'll attach the SOC2 artefacts and a redacted architecture for the VPC flow. I'll put a link in the follow-up — note that some items are NDA gated.
[01:53] Carlos: Also curious about failover — if APAC is live and a region flaps, do you have automatic routing to a different region with warm caches? We can't afford to hit cold-cache p99s across the board.
[02:05] Liam: Routing supports warm standby; we can replicate KV cache to the failover region for certain models but that increases cost. There's a tradeoff — if you want <200ms p99 in failover, that's an extra replication and warm nodes.
[02:20] Carlos: What's the rough cost multiplier for replication?
[02:23] Liam: Ballpark 1.6x for the active+warm standby footprint depending on model size and sequence length. We'll put a precise calc in the spreadsheet.
[02:31] Samir: That could blow our numbers. We'll want options: graceful degradation vs full replication.
[02:36] Maya: Agree — we'll model three options: (A) active-only with cross-region fallback to hosted low-geo (higher latency), (B) active + warm standby replication (higher cost lower latency), (C) hybrid with selective replication for critical endpoints.
[02:50] Nora: Selective replication sounds promising — we only need sub-200ms for our customer-facing agents, internal diagnostics can be relaxed.
[02:57] Maya: Good. On contract amendment — two parts: commit uplift (30%) for next 12 months, and an attached burst pool with monthly usage billing. Samir you mentioned quarter close on 10/20?
[03:09] Samir: Yes need pricing and legal draft before that.
[03:12] Maya: We'll target a draft by 10/15.
[03:15] Liam: Technical note — for the benchmark I will run two profiles: a steady-state 95th percentile test and a flash-burst test to emulate Black Friday-ish patterns. I'll include the exact configs.
[03:25] Carlos: Perfect. Also, can you surface per-token cost breakdowns in the bench? We need token-level to compare to our in-house infra.
[03:33] Liam: Yep, per-token plus per-request latency histograms.
[03:36] Carlos: On the private deployment/VPC path — we have a compliance requirement to keep full audit logs in EU. That means the platform must not export logs outside of their region. Is that doable?
[03:45] Maya: We support region-bound logs for Private deployments; for Hosted we redact and offer log retention options, but for strict residency we recommend Private or Dedicated in-region.
[03:54] Nora: Good. Also, KMS integration — we use HashiCorp Vault right now, could you integrate with our KMS for envelope encryption?
[04:01] Liam: We have a couple integrations: AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and HSM via KMIP; HashiCorp Vault-backed KMS is possible through our customer-managed key gateway but it's a pilot path. Will need network egress rules.
[04:12] Carlos: That may be fine as long as we can demonstrate key separation.
[04:16] Maya: We'll note that as a technical dependency in the amendment.
[04:19] [crosstalk] Samir: Quick question — SLA penalties?
[04:21] Maya: We can add uptime SLOs for Dedicated/Private tiers; Hosted has standard terms but for commits we can talk about uptime credits.
[04:29] Carlos: One more thing on benchmarks — we saw reduced throughput at long sequence lengths for quantized models. Can you include 8-bit and int4 runs?
[04:37] Liam: Yes, I'll include quantized runs. Note that int4 may change output marginally; we'll flag any quality diffs.
[04:45] Nora: We'll need quality regression checks — can Redwood rerun a small eval suite against the quantized outputs?
[04:51] Liam: Yep, if you share 200 reference prompts we can run automatic regression metrics.
[04:55] Carlos: We'll assemble that.
[04:57] Maya: Great. Quick timeline recap: liam bench this weekend, carlos sends peak traces by Mon 10/12, maya draft amendment by 10/15, procurement confirms PO window by 10/20, security docs review scheduled next week.
[05:12] Samir: Sounds good.
[05:15] Nora: Quick nit — do you have a recommended rollout for EU region activation? BlueAnchor prefers phased: logs/audit first, then routing, then full model traffic.
[05:26] Liam: That's the pattern we normally recommend: 1) provision region and VPC, 2) sync logs and KMS, 3) run small pilot traffic ramp, 4) cutover. We'll provide a checklist.
[05:37] Carlos: Any blockers from Redwood's side?
[05:39] Maya: None immediate. We may need a brief network workshop with your infra team — 30-60 minutes — to verify firewall rules and peering for the VPC.
[05:48] Nora: We'll schedule that.
[05:50] Maya: Okay let's capture action items and owners.
[05:53] [00:05:54] Speaker 1: Action items recap — Carlos send peak traces, Liam run bench and share sheet, Maya send contract amendment and SOC2 docs, Nora coordinate network workshop, Samir confirms procurement dates.
[06:08] Carlos: One minute on pricing: can you provide a sample cost scenario showing baseline, baseline+burst, and baseline+replication? A 3-line model we can slot into finance quickly.
[06:20] Maya: We'll include that in the amendment.
[06:23] Samir: And please call out any one-time onboarding fees.
[06:27] Maya: Will do.
[06:30] Carlos: Thanks everyone, this was helpful.
[06:33] Maya: Thanks all. We'll follow up with the benchmark link and the draft amendment.
[06:37] [end recording]

Notes: transcription contains occasional mis-hearings (e.g., 'K-V cash' for KV cache), and speaker labels auto-assigned where needed. Shared artifacts referenced: internal bench spreadsheet (to be sent), contract amendment draft (to be sent), SOC2 pack (link in follow-up).
